question: What is the hermeneutical principle of 'the analogy of faith' (analogia fidei) and how does it guide Catholic Scripture interpretation?

choices.A: Scripture passages must be interpreted in light of the whole coherent content of the faith — no text may be read in isolation against the totality of what God has revealed
choices.B: Only passages that have a clear analogy with the reader's personal experience can be trusted
choices.C: Earlier biblical books always override later ones when there is apparent contradiction
choices.D: Every Scripture text has exactly one literal meaning and all others are rejected

teaching.title: Analogia Fidei — Analogy of Faith
teaching.body: The 'analogy of faith' (Romans 12:6, analogia tes pisteos) refers to the coherent unity of all revealed doctrine. In Catholic hermeneutics (Dei Verbum 12, CCC 114), it means: Scripture is interpreted within the totality of the faith and not in isolation. A passage that seems to contradict an established doctrine must be re-examined in its context before being used to overturn the whole. This principle explains why Catholic exegesis often differs from 'plain reading' approaches — the Church brings the full context of the tradition, the creeds, and the other texts of Scripture to each passage, reading the Bible as a unified whole with Christ as its center.
